                    ### Question
                    An investigator is studying the structural characteristics of pathogenic viruses. Cell cultures infected by different viruses are observed under a scanning electron microscope. One of the cell samples is infected by a virus that has an envelope composed of nuclear membrane molecules. The most likely virus that has infected this cell sample can cause which of the following conditions?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Yellow fever
opb. Shingles
opc. Erythema infectiosum
opd. Ebola
ope. Condylomata acuminata
"

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The virus that uses nuclear membrane molecules for its envelope and is likely to have infected the cell sample is a member of the Herpesviridae family. The Varicella-zoster virus (VZV), which causes shingles, fits this description. This conclusion is supported by evidence linking Human herpesvirus 3, another name for VZV, to Herpes zoster disease.
